Design complete. Root cause confirmed by profiling against the real 492MB DB: per-snapshot re-query over overlapping trailing windows is 59% of classify.py and 99% of lga_leadership.py; scipy/trough detection is 1%.

Decision: both range paths load once and slice, but with different shapes, because memory is the binding constraint on Viking:
- lga_leadership (SQL already aggregates to (date,LGA); full history = 106k rows / 30 MB) -> single full-range _load_lga_sums + date-bucketed searchsorted slicing. Parity provable: HAVING groups on (price_date, council), which no window can split.
- classify (raw per-station rows; full history = 2.23M rows / 540 MB resident, 881 MB peak -> would OOM Viking) -> one ORDER BY price_date scan feeding a 45-day deque of per-day buckets, ~7 MB resident. Yield buckets, not flattened rows.
Single-snapshot paths (the daily daily-db-update.yml path) unchanged in both.

experiments/2026-08-21_tau_cadence/ (README + tau_sweep.csv + tau_sweep.png). 12 tau x 3 cadences off one paid walk-forward fit, 14 folds / 5 stations / seed 42 / 54 cols (54:1a6ec2d84a69), all 36 cells dry-free.

Best-tau-in-hindsight vs production tau=0.25: 7d +0.009, 2d +0.086, 1d +0.062 c/L. The 1d gain is 2% of that cadence's 2.97 c/L headroom. The hypothesis is directionally right and economically irrelevant - the optimum does climb 0.20/0.30/0.35 as the grid refines, and it is worth nothing.

Decisive line is the flip count (acceptance criterion 3), and it inverts the usual reading: at 1d, moving tau 0.25 -> 0.35 changes 422 buy/wait decisions for 0.062 c/L. The changes cancel. That is a real measurement of NO effect, not an underpowered measurement of a real one - much stronger than a small-flip-count null. At 7d the comparable move changes 8 decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Realised CPL vs tau at 1d, same folds/stations/seed/columns: DONE, plus 2d and 7d for contrast.
- Stated verdict: signal-content limit.
- Decision-flip count behind the sub-0.1 c/L deltas: DONE (422 / 132 / 8).
- If tau moves, re-lock recommendation: tau does NOT move. NO re-lock, docs/STATUS.md unchanged.

Method caveat recorded in the README: the sweep picks tau in hindsight, so a flat curve RULES OUT the operating point while a dip would only have upper-bounded a gain. The curve is flat, so the definitive half is the half that applies.

The cap was ALSO an artefact of crude modelling, which is the part worth carrying: the exposure arithmetic charged two draws the FULL texture ICC for sharing even ONE source column. Two draws sharing 1 of 10 columns share about a tenth of their texture, not all of it. Binary charge put a 20-draw arity-10 bank at 2.4 effective draws; the shared-FRACTION charge puts it at 9.04, and the bar then degrades GENTLY at every width (1 col -0.152, 10 cols -0.171, 35 cols -0.287 c/L). That is exactly what fps-3jj.21 said the old design failed to do. The cap was solving a problem the modelling invented.
